Note to self: DPO and REINFORCE difference

The loss function in Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is given by \[ \mathcal L_{DPO} = -E_{(c, y^+, y^-)\sim D^{\text{train}}} [\sigma(\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y^+ | c)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y^+ | c)}) - \log\frac{\pi_\theta(y^- | c)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y^- | c)})]. \] Here the weight updates will not change the distribution \(D^{train}\).

At other times, we may be interested in optimizing the \[ J(\theta) = E_{y\sim\pi_{\theta (\cdot \mid c)}}[R(c,y)]. \] The immediate obstacle for that the sampling distribution depends on \(\theta\). To address this, note that \[ \nabla J(\theta) = \sum_{y}R(c,y)\nabla_\theta \pi_{\theta}(y \mid c) = E_{y\sim \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid c)}[R(c,y)\nabla_\theta\log(\pi_\theta (y \mid c))], \] where the last equality follows from the trick that \(\frac{\partial }{\partial \theta}f_\theta(x) = f_\theta(x)\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log(f_\theta(x))\) under suitable regularity conditions. The advantage brought is that we now can estimate \(\nabla J(\theta)\) by sampling over \(y\sim \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid c)\), rather than emumerating over the potentially monstrous \(y\).

One does not need to know the “log-trick” to discover this useful computation trick. Once we turn to the sampling strategy, the following inverse propensity weighting estimator is almost second nature: \[ E_{y\sim \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid c)}[R(c,y) \frac{\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta (y\mid c)}{\pi_\theta(y\mid c)}]. \] Since \(\frac{\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta (y\mid c)}{\pi_\theta(y\mid c)} =\nabla_\theta\log(\pi_\theta (y \mid c))\), our expression and that appeared in REINFORCE are mathematically equivalent. However, the inverse propensity weighting apporach is less numerically stable.

While here we presented a fixed context/prompt \(c\), in general we assume the context distribution of \(c\) to be fixed, and extension to such case is straightfoward.
